Bots see proportionally to what a player standing in the same spot would: the map's fog of war scaled by the camera zoom there (map default, server /zoom, camera zoom areas) and its full view angle, times a per-difficulty multiplier (BALANCE_BOT_FOV_MULT_*). Before, they had a fixed 1920x1080 box and a 140 degree cone regardless of the map and zoom, extended 1.4x while camping or in combat. Now bot waypoints have a "Look far" camp option: a bot camping there sees like a player with the crosshair at the screen edge - farther, within a much narrower angle. Ordinary camping and combat get the normal view.

The minimap pins an enemy only when they are actually on the observer's screen and within 75% (BALANCE_MINIMAP_SIGHTING_FOV_ANGLE_MULT) of the view angle they effectively have. For you that is your real camera - it follows the crosshair - and the angle narrowed with the edge zoom-out; the range is the zoom-expanded fog of war, so enemies at the edge of a zoomed-out screen get pinned too. A teammate's camera isn't known, so they see what a player standing there would with the default camera settings: the fog of war scaled by the camera zoom at their position and a screen of the fog of war size following their crosshair. The cone follows the crosshair like the drawn fog of war. Heard gunshots are unchanged. The camera's crosshair offset no longer depends on the screen size, which cancelled out anyway.

Camera zoom and the effective fog of war are computed in one place. calc_area_camera_zoom gives the camera zoom at any position (map default, server /zoom, camera zoom areas) and fog_of_war_settings::get_considered the size and angle the camera effectively shows, narrowed at the screen edge. The edge zoom-out and its angle narrowing are balance params instead of a mutable global and two hardcoded copies.
